rulebook.title: MLB Official Baseball Rules (2025 edition; values unchanged for many seasons)
rulebook.text_used: search extracts of verbatim rule copies (baseballrulesacademy.com) and the Appendix drawings; mlb.com was not reachable for direct reading

pitching_distance_m.note: front edge of the pitcher's plate to the rear point of home plate, 60 ft 6 in

mound.note: flat area 6 in in front, 18 in to each side and 22 in behind the rubber; 18 ft diameter mound

home_plate_m.note: 17 in square with two corners cut: 17, 8.5, 8.5, 12, 12 in

batters_box_m.note: 4 x 6 ft, 6 in from each side of the plate; the lines belong to the box

equipment.rule: 2.01 (slope starts 6 in in front of the rubber)

scene.text: The catcher crouches directly behind home plate in the catcher's box; the plate umpire (umpire-in-chief) stands behind the catcher; base umpires stand where they see the bases.
All fielders except the catcher stand in fair territory; with the pitcher on the rubber, two infielders are on each side of second base with both feet on the infield dirt.
Batters, base runners and base coaches wear batting helmets (ear flap); the catcher wears a helmet and mask.
The pitcher's glove is not white or grey (piping excepted) and carries no other-coloured material; nothing is attached to the pitching hand, fingers or wrists (no tape, bandage or bracelet).
Home plate is a white five-sided slab 43 cm wide; the white pitcher's plate (61 x 15 cm) sits on a mound 25 cm above home plate, 18.44 m away.

fouls.title: Pivot foot on the pitcher's plate
fouls.text: In the windup and set positions the pitcher faces the batter with the pivot foot in contact with the pitcher's plate (set: the other foot in front of it); a pitch delivered without the pivot foot in contact is an illegal pitch.
fouls.legal: the pivot foot is on the ground against the pitcher's plate
avoid: pivot foot off the pitcher's rubber at the start of the delivery

fouls.title: No second step or replanted pivot foot
fouls.text: The pitcher may not take a second step toward home plate with either foot or reset the pivot foot during the delivery (balk with runners on, illegal pitch otherwise); the pivot foot may drag.
fouls.legal: the pivot foot drags from the rubber, it does not hop forward and re-plant
avoid: pitcher hopping forward and re-planting the back foot

fouls.title: Balk postures
fouls.text: A balk includes delivering to the batter while not facing the batter, making the pitching motion while not touching the pitcher's plate, and throwing to a base without stepping directly toward it.
fouls.legal: the stride goes straight toward home plate

fouls.title: Pitcher's glove, hand and ball
fouls.text: The glove may not be white or grey or carry other-coloured material; nothing may be attached to the pitching hand or wrist; no foreign substance on the ball.
fouls.legal: a dark glove, a bare pitching hand, a clean white ball
avoid: tape or bandage on the pitching hand

fouls.title: Feet in the batter's box
fouls.text: A batter who hits the ball with one or both feet on the ground entirely outside the batter's box is out; the lines belong to the box.
fouls.legal: both feet are inside the batter's box
avoid: batter's foot outside the chalk box

fouls.title: Batting helmet
fouls.text: Every player at bat or running the bases wears a protective batting helmet.
fouls.legal: the batter wears a batting helmet with an ear flap
avoid: batter wearing a cap instead of a helmet

fouls.title: Strike zone
fouls.text: Over home plate, from the hollow beneath the kneecap up to the midpoint between the top of the shoulders and the top of the uniform pants, judged from the batter's stance.
